title: Dashoguz municipal briefing on ration-eligibility documents
reason: Administrative meeting of neighborhood-management leaders, not a public protest gathering.
notes: The report says municipal officials briefed heads of housing administrations on requiring original passports for ration eligibility. It does not describe a public gathering demanding a state change.

title: Ashgabat women protest demolition of their homes
reason: Outside the assigned January 2021 event month; the article dates the physical gathering to 21 February 2017.
notes: The Azattyq Asia page is dated 22 February 2017 and reports that more than 40 women gathered in Ashgabat at 11 a.m. to demand replacement housing for homes being demolished by authorities. This is retained as a dated scope exclusion, not a January 2021 candidate. The reported count does not establish the >=50 threshold.

title: Women go to the local administration over food shortages in Shatlyk
reason: The physical gathering occurred in February 2021, after the assigned January event month; no direct continuity with the January Bayramali queues is established.
notes: A limited body read reports around 80 women at the local administration in Shatlyk, Mary region, complaining about subsidized-food supply interruptions and a reduction in the bread ration. Regional officials and police arrived and calmed the crowd. The source does not link this action to E005; retain as a later-boundary scope exclusion, not a continuation or January candidate.

title: Women protest bread/flour and water-supply problems at Mary city administration
reason: The physical gathering began on 21 December 2020, outside the assigned January month; Fergana reports that this gathering's participants left that day. Its relation to any later action is not established.
notes: CABAR's 4 January 2021 review and the linked Fergana report describe about 50 women at the Mary city administration on 21 December over bread/flour supply and water problems. Fergana reports police tried to move them; after an official promised to relay their problems to the hyakim, the women left. Both reports cite Radio Azatlyk and are not independent. This establishes a reported physical end for that gathering, but does not rule out or link any separate later January action. The approximate count is not a hard >=50 minimum.
